audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity (tb-025): Log topics tuple MUST have at most 4 elements
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Log topic validation (LOG0-LOG4 opcodes) is an EVM execution layer concept. Prysm is a consensus layer client and does not implement EVM opcode processing, log construction, or log topic validation. No relevant code exists in the Prysm codebase.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity (tb-029): Receipt immutability after construction
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Receipt construction and immutability (slotted_freezable) is an execution layer concept. Prysm only references receipts_root as an opaque Bytes32 field in ExecutionPayloadHeader; it does not construct, validate, or mutate Receipt objects.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity (tb-023): cumulative_gas_used monotonically non-decreasing in Receipt
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. cumulative_gas_used tracking in Receipt is an execution layer concern. Prysm does not construct or validate individual transaction receipts or their gas accounting. The CL only sees the receipts_root hash.

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: Bloom filter consistency with receipt logs
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Bloom filter construction from receipt logs is an execution layer operation. Prysm references logs_bloom only as an opaque ByteVector[256] field in ExecutionPayload protobuf messages received from the EL via Engine API. No bloom filter logic exists in Prysm.

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: Bloom bytearray MUST be exactly 256 bytes
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. The bloom filter size constraint (256 bytes / 2048 bits) is enforced in execution layer clients via the add_to_bloom function. Prysm treats logs_bloom as an opaque fixed-size SSZ ByteVector field; size is enforced by SSZ schema (ssz-size:"256") not by bloom construction logic.

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: bit_to_set in add_to_bloom MUST be in [0, 2047]
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. The add_to_bloom function and its bit_to_set computation (11-bit mask 0x07FF) are execution layer EVM internals. Prysm does not implement bloom filter construction. No add_to_bloom function or equivalent exists in the Prysm codebase (confirmed via tree-sitter search).

audit_items.title: Verify Invariant: byte_index in add_to_bloom MUST be in [0, 255]
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. The byte_index computation in add_to_bloom is an execution layer EVM internal. Prysm does not implement bloom filter construction or manipulation. No relevant code exists in the Prysm codebase.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is GAS_CAP exactly 16777216 (2^24)?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Per-transaction GAS_CAP (16777216) is an execution layer concept enforced in EL txpool and block validation. In Prysm, 16777216 appears only as SSZ max list bounds for historical_roots and historical_summaries (beacon state fields), completely unrelated to transaction gas caps. Prysm does not implement transaction gas limit validation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does txpool reject transactions with gasLimit > 16777216?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Prysm is a consensus layer client and does not implement a transaction pool (txpool). Transaction validation against gas caps is performed by execution layer clients (Geth, Nethermind, etc.). The only txpool reference in Prysm is in end-to-end test configuration for Geth flags.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does P2P-relayed transaction validation match local validation?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Transaction validation (local vs P2P-relayed) is an execution layer concern. Prysm's P2P layer handles beacon blocks, attestations, and other CL messages, not individual transactions. Transaction propagation and validation is handled by the EL client.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does block validation reject blocks with over-cap transactions?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Per-transaction gas cap validation within blocks is an execution layer responsibility. Prysm validates beacon blocks (slot, proposer, attestations, etc.) but delegates execution payload validation to the EL client via the Engine API (engine_newPayloadV*). The CL does not inspect individual transactions within execution payloads.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does block validation check ALL transactions without skipping?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Iterating over and validating all transactions in a block is an execution layer operation. Prysm passes the entire execution payload to the EL via Engine API for validation; it does not iterate over or validate individual transactions.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the entire block rejected when any transaction violates gas cap?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Atomic block rejection based on per-transaction gas cap violations is an execution layer concern. Prysm relies on the EL's engine_newPayload response (VALID/INVALID) for execution payload validity and does not perform per-transaction validation itself.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is per-transaction gas cap independent of block gas limit?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. The relationship between per-transaction gas cap and block gas limit is an execution layer validation concern. Prysm stores gas_limit as a field in ExecutionPayload/Header but does not enforce per-transaction gas caps or compare them to block gas limits.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are both txpool and block validation independently enforcing gas cap?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Defense-in-depth gas cap enforcement at txpool and block validation layers is an execution layer concern. Prysm does not implement either validation layer for transaction gas limits.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gas cap value 16777216 identical at both enforcement points?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Constant consistency between txpool and block validation enforcement points is an execution layer concern. The value 16777216 in Prysm is used only for SSZ list bounds on historical_roots/historical_summaries, not for gas cap enforcement.

audit_items.title: Is a rejected transaction dropped and never forwarded to block building?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Transaction rejection and block building pipeline isolation is an execution layer concern. While Prysm interacts with block builders via the Builder API and has a gas_limit setting for proposals, it does not manage the transaction lifecycle or enforce per-transaction gas caps.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the comparison operator <= (not <) used for gas cap check?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. The comparison operator semantics for gas cap checking (<=, <, >, >=) is an execution layer validation detail. Prysm does not perform any comparison of transaction gasLimit against a gas cap constant.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do all clients use identical comparison semantics?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Cross-client comparison semantics for gas cap enforcement is a cross-EL-client concern. Prysm is a CL client and does not implement gas cap comparison logic. This check should target EL clients (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon, Reth).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is RLP encoding of gasLimit strictly validated?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. RLP encoding validation of transaction gasLimit is an execution layer concern. Prysm uses SSZ encoding for consensus layer objects and protobuf for Engine API communication; it does not parse or validate RLP-encoded transactions.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is per-tx cap enforced even when block gas limit exceeds it?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Per-transaction gas cap enforcement independent of block gas limit is an execution layer validation concern. Prysm does not validate individual transaction gas limits.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gas cap validation O(1) per transaction?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Performance characteristics of gas cap validation is an execution layer concern. Prysm does not implement per-transaction gas cap validation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does block validation catch over-cap transactions from direct block construction?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Block validation of directly-constructed blocks (via Engine API) for gas cap violations is an execution layer concern. While Prysm sends execution payloads via Engine API, the validation of transaction contents within those payloads is performed by the EL client.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does transaction replacement re-validate gasLimit?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Transaction replacement (nonce-based bumping) and re-validation of gasLimit is an execution layer txpool concern. Prysm does not manage a transaction mempool or handle transaction replacement.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gasLimit covered by the transaction signature?
audit_items.reason: Component mismatch: EL vs CL. Transaction signature coverage (which fields are signed) is an execution layer concern defined by EIP-155/EIP-1559/EIP-4844 transaction formats. Prysm does not parse, sign, or verify individual EL transaction signatures.
